context.title: The Last Supper and Arrest
context.summary: Judas agrees to betray Jesus. At the Passover Jesus gives the bread and cup, settles a dispute about greatness, and foretells Peter's denial. He prays on the Mount of Olives, is arrested, and Peter denies him.
context.background: Luke alone mentions a cup both before and after the bread, fitting the several cups of a Passover meal. Verses 43–44, about the angel and the sweat like drops of blood, are missing from some early manuscripts. Luke alone says Jesus healed the servant's ear (v. 51).

customs.note: Carrying water jars was usually women's work, so a man doing it would stand out in a crowded city.

watchFor: 'This cup is the new testament in my blood' (v. 20).
'I am among you as he that serveth' (v. 27).
After the third denial 'the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter' (v. 61).

people.name: Satan
people.summary: Adversary; accuser. When used as a proper name, the Hebrew word so rendered has the article “the adversary” (Job 1:6-12; 2:1-7).

people.name: Judas
people.summary: Son of Simon (John 6:71; 13:2, 26), surnamed Iscariot, i.e., a man of Kerioth (Josh. 15:25). His name is uniformly the last in the list of the apostles, as given in the synoptic (i.e., the first three) Gospels.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: John
people.summary: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” (Matt. 4:21; 10:2; Mark 1:19; 3:17; 10:35). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee (Matt. 4:21) and Salome (Matt. 27:56; comp. Mark 15:40), and was born at Bethsaida.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

places.name: mount of Olives
places.summary: So called from the olive trees with which its sides are clothed, is a mountain ridge on the east of Jerusalem (1 Kings 11:7; Ezek. 11:23; Zech. 14:4), from which it is separated by the valley of Kidron.

events.title: Holy Week
